text: Twenty videos ago, one aging server with no secondary copy cost two days of production scheduling. This is the honest close, not a highlight reel.
What's real: BrennanWSFC and BrennanAG with a proven automatic failover, scheduled automation, a measured performance fix, an off-site backup, a live dashboard, and MongoDB under the same discipline.
What's still honest and named: the new-database checklist still needs a human to follow it, MongoDB has no automatic failover yet, and no true site-level disaster drill has run.
A prioritized list for whoever picks this up next: a real site-level drill first, then a same-day gate for new databases, then scoping Mongo's own failover if it's ever warranted.
A genuinely dangerous single point of failure is gone, replaced by something tested and honestly documented. A finished engagement, not a perfect one -- and that's the whole series.
